This means the lock is held for milliseconds, not minutes.\n1582\t\n1583\t## Heartbeat Protocol\n1584\t\n1585\tEvery worker emits a heartbeat file to enable peer monitoring and stale claim detection.\n1586\t\n1587\t### Heartbeat File\n1588\t\n1589\t```\n1590\t~/.needle/state/heartbeats/<worker-id>.json\n1591\t```\n1592\t\n1593\tContents:\n1594\t\n1595\t```json\n1596\t{\n1597\t  \"worker_id\": \"needle-claude-anthropic-sonnet-alpha\",\n1598\t  \"pid\": 12345,\n1599\t  \"state\": \"EXECUTING\",\n1600\t  \"current_bead\": \"nd-a3f8\",\n1601\t  \"workspace\": \"/home/coder/project\",\n1602\t  \"last_heartbeat\": \"2026-03-20T15:30:00Z\",\n1603\t  \"started_at\": \"2026-03-20T14:00:00Z\",\n1604\t  \"beads_processed\": 7,\n1605\t  \"session\": \"needle-claude-anthropic-sonnet-alpha\"\n1606\t}\n1607\t```\n1608\t\n1609\t### Emission\n1610\t\n1611\t- Heartbeat is emitted every `heartbeat_interval` (default: 30 seconds)\n1612\t- Emitted from a dedicated thread/task, independent of the main worker loop\n1613\t- Updates `last_heartbeat` timestamp and `state` field\n1614\t- File write is atomic (write to temp file, rename)\n1615\t\n1616\t### TTL and Stale Detection\n1617\t\n1618\tA heartbeat is **stale** if `now - last_heartbeat > heartbeat_ttl` (default: 5 minutes).\n1619\t\n1620\tA stale heartbeat means the worker has stopped updating — it has crashed, hung, or been killed.\n1621\t\n1622\t### Peer Monitoring\n1623\t\n1624\tThe Mend strand (Strand 2) checks peer heartbeats:\n1625\t\n1626\t1. Read all heartbeat files in `~/.needle/state/heartbeats/`\n1627\t2. For each stale heartbeat:\n1628\t   a. Check if the PID is still alive (`kill -0 <pid>`)\n1629\t   b. If PID is dead: worker crashed. Clean up.\n1630\t   c. If PID is alive but heartbeat is stale: worker is stuck. Log warning.\n1631\t3. For crashed workers:\n1632\t   a. Release any claimed bead\n1633\t   b. Remove heartbeat file\n1634\t   c. Deregister from worker state registry\n1635\t   d. Emit `peer.crashed` telemetry\n1636\t\n1637\t## Worker State Registry\n1638\t\n1639\tA shared file tracks all active workers for fleet-level awareness.\n1640\t\n1641\t```\n1642\t~/.needle/state/workers.json\n1643\t```\n1644\t\n1645\tContents:\n1646\t\n1647\t```json\n1648\t{\n1649\t  \"workers\": [\n1650\t    {\n1651\t      \"id\": \"needle-claude-anthropic-sonnet-alpha\",\n1652\t      \"pid\": 12345,\n1653\t      \"workspace\": \"/home/coder/project\",\n1654\t      \"agent\": \"claude\",\n1655\t      \"model\": \"sonnet\",\n1656\t      \"started_at\": \"2026-03-20T14:00:00Z\",\n1657\t      \"beads_processed\": 7\n1658\t    }\n1659\t  ],\n1660\t  \"updated_at\": \"2026-03-20T15:30:00Z\"\n1661\t}\n1662\t```\n1663\t\n1664\t**Access pattern:**\n1665\t- Workers register on startup, deregister on shutdown\n1666\t- Registry is updated via flock-protected read-modify-write\n1667\t- Used by `needle list`, `needle status`, and fleet-level telemetry\n1668\t- Not used for coordination — heartbeats handle that\n1669\t\n1670\t## Concurrency Limits\n1671\t\n1672\t### Provider/Model Limits\n1673\t\n1674\tRate limiting prevents API throttling and controls cost:\n1675\t\n1676\t```yaml\n1677\tlimits:\n1678\t  launch_stagger_seconds: 2          # delay between worker launches\n1679\t  providers:\n1680\t    anthropic:\n1681\t      max_concurrent: 10             # max workers using Anthropic simultaneously\n1682\t      requests_per_minute: 60\n1683\t    openai:\n1684\t      max_concurrent: 5\n1685\t      requests_per_minute: 40\n1686\t  models:\n1687\t    claude-sonnet:\n1688\t      max_concurrent: 8\n1689\t    claude-opus:\n1690\t      max_concurrent: 3              # expensive model, limit concurrency\n1691\t```\n1692\t\n1693\t**Enforcement:**\n1694\t- Before dispatching to an agent, the worker checks the provider/model concurrency counters\n1695\t- If at limit, the worker waits with backoff (not the same as strand exhaustion — there is work, just rate limited)\n1696\t- Counters are maintained in the worker state registry\n1697\t- RPM limits are enforced via a token bucket per provider (stored in `~/.needle/state/rate_limits/`)\n1698\t\n1699\t### Fleet Sizing\n1700\t\n1701\tThe practical worker limit is not an arbitrary number. It is driven by three runtime constraints:\n1702\t\n1703\t1. **Provider inference throughput.** Each worker waiting on an LLM response is idle CPU but an active API slot. If the provider rate-limits or queues requests, adding workers produces no additional throughput. NEEDLE tracks RPM per provider and warns when request latency exceeds a threshold.\n1704\t\n1705\t2. **Available CPU.** Each agent process (Claude Code, OpenCode, etc.) consumes CPU during tool execution, file I/O, and git operations. NEEDLE's own overhead (strand evaluation, heartbeat I/O, lock contention) also scales with worker count. When system load exceeds a configurable threshold, NEEDLE emits a `fleet.cpu_saturated` warning.\n1706\t\n1707\t3. **Available RAM.** Each agent process holds context in memory. Agent processes with large context windows or many tool calls can consume significant RAM. NEEDLE monitors system memory and warns when free memory drops below a threshold.\n1708\t\n1709\t`max_workers` is a configurable ceiling, not a recommendation. The right value depends on the environment:\n1710\t\n1711\t```yaml\n1712\tworker:\n1713\t  max_workers: 0              # 0 = no hard ceiling, rely on runtime monitoring\n1714\t  cpu_load_warn: 0.8          # warn when system load average > 80% of cores\n1715\t  memory_free_warn_mb: 512    # warn when free memory < 512MB\n1716\t```\n1717\t\n1718\tIf `max_workers` is set, it is enforced at launch time. `needle run --count=25` with `max_workers: 20` will launch 20 and log a warning. If set to 0, NEEDLE launches the requested count and relies on runtime monitoring to signal saturation.\n1719\t\n1720\t## Race Condition Prevention\n1721\t\n1722\tLessons from `docs/notes/claim-race-conditions.md`, applied to the new design:\n1723\t\n1724\t| Race Condition | v1 Impact | v2 Prevention |\n1725\t|---------------|-----------|---------------|\n1726\t| **Thundering herd** | All workers claim same bead | Per-workspace flock serializes claims |\n1727\t| **TOCTOU on closed beads** | Worker claims bead that was just closed | Verify bead status inside flock before claiming |\n1728\t| **Stale claims from crashed workers** | Beads stuck `in_progress` forever | Heartbeat TTL + Mend strand auto-release |\n1729\t| **Lock file leaks** | Orphaned locks block claims | Lock TTL + Mend strand cleanup |\n1730\t| **Concurrent bead creation** | (Weave/Pulse/Unravel) create duplicates | Seen-issue deduplication + creation cooldowns |\n1731\t\n1732\t## Concurrency Invariants\n1733\t\n1734\t1. **One claim at a time per workspace.** The flock guarantees this. Two workers cannot execute `br update --claim` simultaneously in the same workspace.\n1735\t\n1736\t2. **One bead per worker.** A worker holds at most one claimed bead. It releases or verifies closure before claiming another.\n1737\t\n1738\t3. **Claims have a TTL.** If a worker holds a claim for longer than `heartbeat_ttl` without updating its heartbeat, the claim is considered stale and eligible for release by Mend.\n1739\t\n1740\t4. **No implicit locking.** Labels are not locks. Bead status is not a lock. Only flock and `br update --claim` provide mutual exclusion.\n1741\t\n1742\t5. **Lock scope is minimal.** The workspace flock is held for milliseconds (duration of the `br` CLI call), never for the duration of bead execution.\n1743\t\n1744\t---\n1745\t\n1746\t# Telemetry\n1747\t\n1748\tEvery state transition, claim attempt, dispatch, and outcome emits structured telemetry. A silent worker is a broken worker.\n1749\t\n1750\t## Telemetry Design Principles\n1751\t\n1752\t1. **Structured from origin.** Events are typed structs, not log strings. They are serialized to JSONL for storage and consumption. Every design decision in this plan traces back to one or more of them.\n\n1. **Deterministic order.** Given the same queue state, every worker computes the same bead ordering. There is no randomness in selection. Ties are broken by creation time.\n\n2. **Explicit outcome paths.** Every possible result of every operation has a named handler. If an outcome can happen, it has a handler. If it doesn't have a handler, it cannot happen. The type system enforces exhaustiveness.\n\n3. **Platform and model agnostic.** NEEDLE wraps any headless CLI that accepts a prompt and exits. It runs on any POSIX system. It does not depend on any specific AI provider, model, or API.\n\n4. **Observable by default.** Every state transition, claim attempt, dispatch, and outcome emits structured telemetry. A silent worker is a broken worker. Telemetry is structured from origin (JSONL) and exportable as OpenTelemetry (OTLP) so any compliant backend — Tempo, Jaeger, Grafana, Honeycomb, Datadog, FABRIC — can consume NEEDLE's signals without a custom adapter.\n\n5. **Self-healing.** Workers detect and recover from stuck states, stale claims, crashed peers, and corrupted databases without human intervention. Recovery paths are explicit, not heuristic.\n\n6. **Separation of concerns.** The orchestrator does not execute work. The agent does not manage state. The bead store does not enforce workflow. Each component has one job.\n\n---\n\n## Architecture Overview\n\nNEEDLE is composed of five layers:\n\n```\n┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│                        CLI Layer                              │\n│  needle run | stop | list | attach | status | config          │\n├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n│                     Worker Layer                              │\n│  Worker loop, strand waterfall, session management            │\n├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n│   Agent Layer                                 │\n│  Adapter interface, dispatch, result capture                  │\n├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n│                   Foundation Layer                             │\n│  Telemetry, configuration, bead store interface, self-healing │\n└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n```\n\n### Decision\n\nThe implementation language must provide:\n\n| Requirement | Why | Source |\n|-------------|-----|--------|\n| Exhaustive pattern matching | Every outcome must be handled; compiler `tokio` for async, single binary via static linking, cross-compilation. The beads ecosystem already has Rust precedent (beads_rust, beads-polis).\n\n**Acceptable alternative: Go.** Simpler learning curve, good concurrency, single binary.
